selected_problem: After the canonical gitRemoteDelivery path became base-bound, the exported githubMergePullRequest helper still delegated valid-head calls with no expectedBaseSha to the legacy head-only merge. A direct caller could therefore bypass the new base-integrity protection.

execution.route_basis: Fresh evidence made the direct-helper bypass the highest-priority actionable truth boundary while the wider equal-severity portfolio kept artifact pressure high; no artificial mode rotation was introduced.

changes: githubMergePullRequest now preserves the existing expected-head validation order, then requires expectedBaseSha before any GitHub request for a valid-head merge.
Direct merge calls with a valid expected head but no expected base fail closed with EXPECTED_BASE_SHA_REQUIRED and no external side effect.
Existing merge receipt tests now bind a base SHA and exercise the new PR-base preflight before the merge PUT.
The remote-provider regression suite now proves missing-base rejection, expected-base receipt preservation, and continued credential redaction.

validation.pre_fix_reproduction: REPRODUCED: the fresh-main direct helper accepted a valid expected head with no expected base and immediately issued PUT /pulls/10/merge, returning ok=true.
validation.node_checks: PASS: core/git.mjs, core/git-base.mjs and three focused test files

truth_boundaries: Direct and canonical remote merge entry points now both require or derive a base identity before a valid merge can proceed.

BLOCKED_EXTERNAL: GitHub's merge REST endpoint still lacks an atomic expected-base-SHA precondition, so a base change between the final read and merge PUT cannot be eliminated by client-side checks alone.
No force push, repository-rule bypass, credential exposure, payment, formal Release, or destructive/irreversible action is introduced.
